items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: But Jack Benny was funny of course. I’d never heard of him

ctx.x: On a cruise? On a ship?

Yeah. And I went on that and my mother had worked there years ago as a secretary in a YMCA or something like that, and she told me how those people, it was laid out like a checkerboard, the numbered streets versus the avenues. And also I got arrangements that I could live at the YMCA on 23rd Street and Sixth Avenue for a dollar a night. And I also could eat in Horn, Harrod, those things, put money in the machine and get food out. They didn’t have a restaurant there. It was my first experience with a cafeteria.…

That was the series between the Yankees and the St. Louis Cardinals, and that was a famous ... I went to the opening game and sat in the bleachers for a dollar and ten cents, sat with a man who worked for the Diamond Match Company. I’ve never seen him since but he was very nice and he said “you coming back tomorrow?” And I said “yes I’d like to come again tomorrow.” “Well I’ll look for you here.” But he said “I live at the” some hotel. He said “come up to see me about eleven o’clock tomorrow, we’ll go together.”…
